## What Is Medical Speech-to-Text Software?


Medical speech-to-text software converts spoken clinical language into accurate written text. HIPAA compliance is a baseline requirement, not a feature.


The category spans three distinct product types that readers often conflate:


-


Real-time front-end dictation: the clinician speaks, text appears immediately in any application, with no lag between thought and documentation


-


Back-end transcription APIs: developer-facing services for batch or streaming audio processing (Amazon Transcribe Medical falls here)


-


Ambient AI scribes: passive tools that capture an entire patient encounter and generate notes afterward


This article focuses on real-time front-end dictation tools, the ones a clinician can install today and use in their next appointment, with no custom software development required.


## How We Ranked Medical Dictation Software


Six criteria determine how tools rank here.


-


**Zero-edit rate:** How often the complete output is usable without touching a single word, which captures clinical utility better than per-word accuracy alone.


-


**Medical vocabulary recognition:** Drug names, anatomical terms, procedure codes, and specialty abbreviations recognized correctly on the first pass.


-


**Latency:** at ~200ms, text appears near-instantly. At 700ms or more, there is a noticeable pause that many clinicians report as disruptive to documentation rhythm.


-


**Compliance posture:** HIPAA eligibility, SOC 2 Type II certification, zero data retention, and signed BAA availability.


-


**Cross-platform support:** Windows workstations at nursing stations, Macs in administrative roles, and iOS for bedside capture.


-


**Pricing structure:** Per-minute API billing, flat subscription, or genuinely unlimited free access.

## Dragon Medical One


Dragon Medical One is Nuance's (a Microsoft company) cloud dictation product for healthcare, sold through authorized resellers and positioned for enterprise health systems already embedded in the Microsoft ecosystem. For a full comparison of[medical speech recognition software](https://willowvoice.com/blog/medical-speech-recognition-software) , Dragon sits alongside several other enterprise options.


### What They Offer


Dragon Medical One provides direct voice integration with Epic and Cerner, medical vocabulary across major specialties recognized without manual setup, a HIPAA BAA included in the subscription, and an optional Dragon Copilot add-on for ambient AI note drafting.


Pricing starts at approximately $99 per user per month on a one-year term, with a $525 per-user implementation fee (as reported by authorized resellers; actual fees vary by contract), putting[first-year cost near $1,713 per clinician](https://checkthat.ai/brands/dragon-medical-one-usa/pricing) based on reseller-published rates, though enterprise contracts may differ, before hardware, EHR integration work, or Citrix licensing. Dragon Medical One runs on Windows only, with no native Mac application. Mac clinicians must use browser-based access or a virtual machine, adding both cost and friction in mixed-device clinical environments.


## Amazon Transcribe Medical


Amazon Transcribe Medical is a HIPAA-eligible AWS API service that adds medical speech recognition to developer-built applications. It is a building block for software vendors, not a plug-and-play tool a clinician can install and use before the next appointment.


### What They Offer


Amazon Transcribe Medical is a HIPAA-eligible ASR service supporting both batch and[streaming transcription modes](https://aws.amazon.com/transcribe/medical/) at[$0.075 per minute](https://aws.amazon.com/transcribe/pricing/) , with a stateless architecture that stores no audio or output text by default.


Good for healthcare engineering teams already operating within AWS that need a medical ASR API to embed inside their own clinical applications or EHR integrations. Teams that need to[voice type medical terms and technical jargon](https://willowvoice.com/blog/dictate-technical-jargon-medical-terms-code-without-errors) without errors will find API-only tools require substantial setup before they can voice a single term.


The core limitation is architectural. There is no Mac, Windows, or iOS application. Getting a single clinician to first dictation requires AWS account management, IAM configuration, and custom software development. For practices without a dedicated engineering team, that infrastructure overhead is the entire barrier.


For healthcare engineering teams building clinical applications inside AWS, Transcribe Medical provides a credible HIPAA-eligible ASR foundation. For individual clinicians or practice managers who need to start documenting now, Willow Voice runs on Mac, Windows, and iOS with no infrastructure setup, medical vocabulary recognized from the first session, and a signed BAA available at the Enterprise tier.


## Apple Dictation


Apple Dictation ships on every Mac and iOS device at no cost. For general-purpose typing, that's a meaningful starting point.


### What It Offers


Apple Dictation offers free system-wide dictation on macOS Tahoe (version 26) with silence-triggered auto-stop and no hard session-length cap. On Apple Silicon, processing runs on-device for standard languages, so general dictation works without a network connection. Basic voice commands handle punctuation and paragraph breaks across native apps like Mail, Pages, and Safari.


It works well for clinicians who want to try voice input for non-clinical tasks like quick emails or general administrative notes before committing to a dedicated medical tool.


Apple does not offer a Business Associate Agreement. Where dictation is processed via Apple servers rather than on-device, that makes it unsuitable for Protected Health Information under HIPAA. On Apple Silicon, standard languages use on-device processing, but clinicians should verify which mode is active for their specific workflow before using Apple Dictation with PHI. For a deeper look at what compliance posture to require from any[voice dictation security and privacy](https://willowvoice.com/blog/voice-dictation-security-privacy-guide) standpoint, see our full guide.


The bottom line: Apple Dictation works for general writing but cannot meet the compliance or vocabulary requirements clinical documentation demands. Willow Voice covers both, with medical terminology recognized from the first session, a zero data retention architecture as a baseline default, and a signed BAA available at the Enterprise tier.


## AWS HealthScribe


The core distinction between the two: Amazon Transcribe Medical is a transcription-only service that converts speech to text at $0.075 per minute, while AWS HealthScribe adds speaker diarization, clinical entity extraction, and AI-generated note summarization on top of transcription at $0.10 per minute, about one-third more per minute. Choose Transcribe Medical when you need raw, accurate medical ASR to feed into your own downstream pipeline; choose HealthScribe when your application needs the full encounter-to-note workflow handled in a single API call and the higher per-minute cost is worth the reduced engineering work.


### What They Offer


AWS HealthScribe provides turn-by-turn transcription with speaker role identification, clinical entity extraction, and AI-generated preliminary note summaries across batch and[real-time streaming modes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/health-scribe.html) , HIPAA-eligible at $0.10 per minute, available in the US East (N. Virginia) region only.


Good for healthcare software vendors and engineering teams building clinical documentation applications who need a single HIPAA-eligible API combining transcription, speaker diarization, entity extraction, and note summarization inside AWS.


The same infrastructure barrier that applies to Amazon Transcribe Medical applies here: no standalone app, no Mac or Windows client, no iOS keyboard. Reaching first dictation requires AWS account setup, IAM configuration, and software development before any note gets captured. Generated notes are probabilistic drafts requiring clinical review before entering patient records. Clinicians who need to start documenting today should look elsewhere.

## FAQs


### How do I choose between Willow Voice, Dragon Medical One, and Amazon Transcribe Medical for clinical documentation?


Start with deployment context: Willow Voice and Dragon Medical One are ready to use today. From there, weigh platform needs (Dragon Medical One is Windows-only) and budget. Dragon's first-year cost runs near $1,713 per clinician, while Willow Voice offers an unlimited free plan.


### Is Willow Voice better than Dragon Medical One for mixed-device clinical environments with both Windows and Mac?


For practices running both Windows and Mac, Willow Voice has a structural advantage: native apps on Mac, Windows, and iOS with the same medical vocabulary and compliance posture on every device. Dragon Medical One is Windows-native and requires browser-based access or a virtual machine for Mac clinicians.


### What does "zero-edit rate" mean, and why does it matter more than raw accuracy for clinical dictation?


Zero-edit rate measures how often a full dictation needs no correction. A 95% zero-edit rate means 95 out of 100 dictations are usable on the first pass, meaningfully different from a tool that hits 95% word accuracy but still requires edits on nearly every note.
